expectations.text: States his newspaper ads cost about $84 to bring in a new customer whose purchase made only about $20 profit, so advertising did not pay
expectations.evidence: says it won't invent figures; no $84

expectations.text: Describes cutting the catalogue to shirtings only and offering a 10 percent mail-reorder discount, raising mail sales from about $100,000 to $700,000
Mentions the name 'The Custom Shop' was a mistake (impersonal) and/or the 'devised a method' window ad fueled rumors the shirts were not really custom
Mentions failure to develop a second-in-command / succession or staff turnover problems
Mentions the failed executive image-consultation program as his biggest disappointment
Turns these into practical marketing advice (test and measure, publicity like Silver Palate, pass savings to customers)
expectations.evidence: general advice: track every advertising dollar against sales
